newsitem.title: NIGERIA: MOBIL SEES NIGERIA OSO CONDENSATE BACK NEXT WEEK.
newsitem.headline: MOBIL SEES NIGERIA OSO CONDENSATE BACK NEXT WEEK.

text.p: Repairs at Mobil Corp's Nigerian Oso condensate field are taking longer than first thought and production is unlikely to resume before next week, company officials said on Wednesday.
"It is a matter of making sure that all valves are carefully checked one by one before we can bring the field back to production. We hope that will be next week," one official in Lagos told Reuters.
Other officials said it was too early to say whether force majeure would have to be extended or any cargoes cancelled.
The company on Friday said it had issued letters of force majeure to lifters of the condensate, informing them of delays in loading because of a longer than expected shutdown.
A technical failure prompted a shutdown of the 100,000 barrels per day (bpd) condensate field, a joint venture with Nigerian National Petroleum Corp, almost two weeks ago.

Nigeria's production of condensate, an extra-light hydrocarbon which is not counted as part of the country's 1.865 million bpd OPEC quota, is expected to reach 200,000 bpd when stage two of the NNPC/Mobil project comes on stream early next year.
